app.title: Literature Review Generator
app.tagline: Eight reviewed stages from a topic to a cited literature review, on Directed Growing Sheet.

form.heading: Start a literature review
form.intro: Describe the topic. You approve the scope before the search starts; everything after runs on its own and can be followed in the workflow viewer.
form.topicPlaceholder: e.g. Irony and narrative voice in Jane Austen's novels
form.notesPlaceholder: Focus, things to leave out, the readers, the length ...
form.budget: Up to about {calls} model calls for the eight stages (their step limits grow with the number of papers), plus up to {graph} for each skill graph a stage runs. Most reviews need fewer; check your provider's rate limits and prices.
form.designGraphs: Stages may design their own graphs
form.designGraphsHelp: When none of a skill's saved graphs fits, the search, screening, organizing and writing stages may plan a graph of steps for this review. You review every graph before it runs and decide whether to save it for later reviews.

run.confirmDelete: Delete this review and its files?
run.cancelling: The run stops before its next model call.

approval.heading: Approve the scope
approval.intro: The search starts once you approve. To change something, write what to change and send it back: the model revises the scope and asks again.
approval.title: Working title
approval.commentPlaceholder: What should change? e.g. Also include criticism written in Chinese.

viewer.heading: Workflow
viewer.idleHint: The eight stages of every review. Click a stage to see what it does.

report.empty: The text appears here once the writing stage has started.
report.checkOk: Check passed: every citation is an included paper of the library.
report.draftNote: Draft: the review is still being written.

issues.unknown_citation: Citations of papers that are not in the library
issues.cites_not_included: Citations of papers that were not included
issues.included_not_cited: Included papers that are never cited
issues.missing_sections: Sections of the outline not written yet

report.blockingHeading: Not finished: the review stage must fix these first.

settings.heading: Settings
settings.openalexHelp: OpenAlex works without a key, with a shared daily budget. A free key from openalex.org gives you your own budget. It is stored only on this computer.
settings.keysHelp: Saved only on this computer (.lrg/config.json) and sent only to their service. Enter or change a key in the AI model section of a new review.

skills.heading: Skills and sample graphs
skills.intro: Stages open these skills for guidance. Each skill has a sample graph for one kind of review that a stage can run as a child graph; it then appears in the viewer under that stage.

literature-search.name: Doing a literature search
literature-search.description: Queries from concepts and synonyms, choosing sources, reviews, classics and recent work, filling gaps.

screening-extraction.name: Screening and extraction
screening-extraction.description: Criteria with exclusion codes, recorded decisions, comparable notes for every included paper.

review-organization.name: Organizing a review
review-organization.description: Themes, methods, chronology or debates; grouping, comparing and finding gaps.

review-writing.name: Writing a review
review-writing.description: Structure, synthesis instead of summary, careful claims, Chinese academic writing.

graphs.chinese-gbt7714: A review in Chinese with GB/T 7714 references

scope.name: Scope
scope.desc: Research questions, criteria and search queries; you approve them.

search.name: Search
search.desc: Searches OpenAlex and arXiv; every result goes into the library.

screen.name: Screen
screen.desc: Includes or excludes each candidate, with a reason.

extract.name: Extract
extract.desc: Notes on method, data, findings and limitations of each included paper.

organize.name: Organize
organize.desc: Groups the papers into themes and compares them.

outline.name: Outline
outline.desc: Plans the sections and which papers each cites.

write.name: Write
write.desc: Writes the sections, citing papers from the library.

review.name: Review
review.desc: Checks citations and coverage, revises, writes the abstract.

errors.no_model: Choose the AI model at the top of the form first.
errors.network: The app does not answer. Is python run.py still running?
errors.no_key: No API key is saved for this service. Enter it in the AI model section.

model.heading: AI model
model.refresh: Ask the service again for its models
model.keyNote: Stored only on this computer and sent only to {service}.
model.keyOptional: Only if the API needs one. Stored only on this computer.
model.loading: Asking the service which models your key can use …
model.needKey: Enter the API key to see the models this key can use.
model.listFailed: The model list could not be loaded: {error}
model.demo: Demo mode: a scripted model, no AI and no key.

graphs.commentPlaceholder: Optional: why not, or what the stage should do instead.
graphs.steps: Each step: what it may do and its instructions
graphs.designedTitle: The {stage} stage designed a graph for this review
graphs.designedIntro: It runs as a child graph of the stage. Each step may only use the permissions shown, and none more than the stage itself has. Approve to run it; reject (with a comment, if you like) to have the stage continue without it.
graphs.runSavedIntro: The {stage} stage wants to run this graph from the skill “{skill}”. Approve to run it; reject to have the stage work without it.
graphs.saveTitle: Save this graph into the skill “{skill}”?
graphs.saveIntro: The graph worked in this review. Saved, it is offered to later reviews (with its run history), and the start page lists it, where you can remove it again.
graphs.scenario: When to use it (saved with the graph in “{skill}”)
graphs.confirmRemove: Remove the saved graph “{title}”? Later reviews will no longer be offered it.

allowances.lrg-search-only: may search OpenAlex and arXiv and list the library
allowances.lrg-screen-only: may read the library and include or exclude papers
allowances.lrg-note-only: may read the library and save notes
allowances.lrg-tag-only: may read the library and assign themes
allowances.lrg-write-only: may read the library and outline and write sections
